newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slip on profit-taking.

text.p: Austrian shares ended weaker on Tuesday after profit-taking undermined a positive start.
Traders saw the blue-chip ATX index well supported just below current levels, however, and forecast a period of sideways trading.
The ATX closed 15.63 points, or 1.08 percent, down at 1,436.48 -- well below the intra-day high of 1,461.27. Market participants pitched support at 1,430.
"It is better to make hay while the sun shines," said a trader, referring to the decision by some funds to take profits now out of the recent rally.
Fears of an imminent hike in German interest rates were also weighing on share prices, other market participants said.
Nevertheless, the underlying mood in Vienna remained upbeat. "The upward trend has not been broken," said a dealer.
Overall five ATX shares finished higher, 14 lower and two unchanged. August ATX futures ended 21 points down at 1,430.0.
Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm was the top gainer, up 0.77 percent at 1,015.90 schillings.
Leading loser was viscose fibre Lenzing, down 5.43 percent at 870 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index slipped 4.86 points, or 0.93 percent, to 518.04.
